# SSH-007: X11 and agent forwarding are off

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** low
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

On a server nobody needs X11 forwarding, and agent forwarding lets anyone with root on the server use the agent of whoever is logged in to reach other machines. Ubuntu's default sshd_config turns X11Forwarding on.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo sshd -T | grep -Ei '^(x11forwarding|allowagentforwarding)'
```

## How to fix it

Set X11Forwarding no and AllowAgentForwarding no; use ProxyJump instead of agent forwarding.

## What a fix can break

Workflows that forward an agent through the server (git over SSH from the server with the laptop's key) stop working.

Run `stackward explain SSH-007` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
